meta.title: Better Scholar: your authorship and venue ranks on Google Scholar
meta.description: A free Chrome extension that marks your role (first, co-first, second, last author) and the CCF / CORE rank of the venue on every paper of a Google Scholar profile, and sums it up in one table.
hero.title: See where you stand on every paper
hero.sub: A Chrome extension for Google Scholar profiles. It marks your authorship role and the venue's CCF / CORE rank on each paper, and adds up the result in one table: “4 first-author CCF-A papers”.
hero.note: Free and open source · Chrome and other Chromium browsers · 30 languages
shot.title: How it looks
shot.caption: An invented profile (real venues, made-up papers): rows coloured by role, rank chips beside each venue, the summary on the right.
shot2.caption: The settings page: choose what is shown, with a live preview.
f.roles.title: Every paper, coloured by your role
f.roles.text: First, co-first, second and last author rows each get a colour, and your name is marked in the author line.
f.ranks.title: CCF and CORE ranks
f.ranks.text: The CCF 2026 and ICORE 2026 rank beside each venue, with the rule that matched it. A venue it cannot place stays unmarked: never a guess.
f.summary.title: A role × rank table
f.summary.text: Pick a cell to list just those papers, and copy the summary or the list for a CV or a grant form.
f.awards.title: Awards and talks
f.awards.text: Best papers, test-of-time awards, Oral, Spotlight and Highlight, from the authors' own words and from the official award pages of over 7,000 papers.
f.complete.title: Cut-off author lists, completed
f.complete.text: Scholar hides the last authors of long lists. One click reads them from the paper's page, or from Semantic Scholar if you allow it.
f.merge.title: Duplicates merged
f.merge.text: If you switch it on, entries that list one paper twice become one, with the citations added up.
f.yours.title: Yours to shape
f.yours.text: Choose what is shown, pick your own colours, hide the parts of Scholar's page you do not need.
f.private.title: Private by design
f.private.text: No account, no analytics, no tracking. Everything is computed in your browser, and the rank lists ship inside the extension.
install.title: Install
install.step1: Download the project from GitHub (the green Code button, then Download ZIP) and unzip it.
install.step2: Open chrome://extensions and turn on Developer mode.
install.step3: Click “Load unpacked” and choose the src folder. Then open any Google Scholar profile.
install.note: A Chrome Web Store listing may follow. Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers work the same way.
honest.title: Honest about its limits
honest.text: Ranks are today's lists, not the rank at the time of publication, and the CCF list itself says it is not an evaluation. The extension never guesses a venue: what it cannot place is listed, not marked.
demo.title: Try it
demo.hint: Switch the roles on and off: the sample profile follows, like the real page.
demo.search: Search papers or use operators: >1000, ccf:a, role:first...
export.title: 1-Click Academic Export
export.note: Ready-to-paste publication lists for CVs, grant forms, LaTeX documents, AI agents and spreadsheets.
ops.title: Instant search and query operators
ops.note: Press [/] anywhere on a Scholar profile to search the whole list at once.
ops.cite.title: Citation thresholds
ops.cite.text: Keep papers with more or fewer citations than any number you type.
ops.tier.title: Venue rank tiers
ops.tier.text: Show only papers in CCF or CORE ranked conferences and journals.
ops.role.title: Authorship roles
ops.role.text: Filter by first, co-first, second or last (senior) author.
ops.year.title: Publication years
ops.year.text: Papers published after, before or within the years you choose.
ops.honors.title: Awards and talks
ops.honors.text: Find Best Paper, Test of Time, Oral, Spotlight and Highlight papers.
ops.reset.title: One-key reset
ops.reset.text: Clears every search, table selection and filter at once.
